overview: Carpenters build and repair the wooden frameworks and structures in homes, offices, bridges and more. They read plans, measure and mark materials, cut and shape wood and install walls, floors, stairs and cabinets. O*NET rates knowledge of building and construction at 4.66 out of 5 for this job and mathematics at 3.91. Most learn on the job or through an apprenticeship; 52% have a high school diploma in O*NET data. The BLS May 2025 median is $60,580 across 670,090 jobs, one of the largest skilled trades. Work is physical, on your feet and often outdoors.
pay: Carpenters earn a median of $60,580, and the top 10% earn $99,910 or more. Hawaii has the highest state median at $85,280, 41% above the national figure, followed by Illinois and California. California also has the most carpenters, 100,750, while Florida has 39,300 at a lower median of $49,870.

faq.a: The BLS May 2025 median is $60,580 a year. The lowest 10% earn under $40,410 and the top 10% earn $99,910 or more, often union carpenters or business owners. Hawaii, Illinois ($79,000) and California ($75,920) pay the most, while Arkansas and Oklahoma pay the least.

faq.q: How do you become a carpenter?
faq.a: Most carpenters learn on the job or through a paid apprenticeship of about 3 to 4 years. In O*NET data, 52% have a high school diploma, 22% a post-secondary certificate and 18% less than a high school diploma. Math and blueprint reading help you progress faster.

faq.q: Is carpentry hard on your body?
faq.a: Yes. In O*NET data, carpenters rank above 94% of U.S. jobs for time on their feet and above 85% for outdoor work in all weather. Tight deadlines are common too. Good safety habits, lifting technique and rest matter for a long career.

Close matches include metal and plastic layout workers (85%), structural metal fabricators (81%) and Riggers (76%), based on O*NET 31.0. Layout Workers earn $63,870, 5% more than carpenters, according to BLS May 2025. Many carpenters also move into supervision or start their own business.
